ideas_for_us.title: Why Your Brain Remembers Embarrassing Moments at 3 AM
ideas_for_us.public_domain_source: The Principles of Psychology by William James (1890)
ideas_for_us.hook: Ever wonder why your brain forces you to relive cringey memories right before you sleep? Science explained it back in 1890.
ideas_for_us.angle: Explaining the survival brain's hyper-fixation on negative memories using early functional psychology.

ideas_for_us.title: 3 Body Language Signs Someone Is Secretly Jealous of You
ideas_for_us.public_domain_source: The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals by Charles Darwin (1872)
ideas_for_us.hook: People try to hide envy, but their faces instantly betray them. Here is the 150-year-old psychological trick to spot it.
ideas_for_us.angle: Revealing micro-expressions of envy and hostility through classic evolutionary observation.

ideas_for_us.title: How to Turn Off Anger Instantly (According to 19th-Century Science)
ideas_for_us.public_domain_source: Outlines of Psychology by Wilhelm Wundt (1897)
ideas_for_us.hook: When someone mocks you, your brain undergoes a rapid physical shift. Here is how to stop it cold.
ideas_for_us.angle: Using foundational experimental psychology to teach emotional mastery and impulse control when insulted.

ideas_for_us.title: What Happens to Your Mind During a Trance or Deep Prayer
ideas_for_us.public_domain_source: The Varieties of Religious Experience by William James (1902)
ideas_for_us.hook: What actually happens to your consciousness when you close your eyes and pray? The founder of American psychology investigated.
ideas_for_us.angle: Deconstructing spiritual and meditative brain states using early neuro-psychological theories.
